note: Project-local source inventory. The repository root evidence policy remains controlling; source class and operational states are separate. For a historical source served through a modern digital presentation, evidenceClass describes the underlying source when stated, while accessState and rightsState describe what is actually accessed and can be reused.

sources.title: DBNL colophon for the 1676 Uyt-spanningen transcription

sources.title: Uyt-spanningen — critical edition and apparatus (2005)

sources.title: I. Hert-sterckte in Jehova, Op 1 Sam. 30:6 — critical-edition item 34

sources.title: II. Hert-sterckte in Jehova — selected text in a 1971 anthology
sources.type: Later anthology / bloemlezing presenting the second Rees song

The 1727 ninth edition prints 1674, which corroborates the date but does not prove what the 1676 compositor set.
The date claim is specifically held in CLM-HERT-II-DATE-1674; other textual claims from this page must be assessed individually.

sources.title: Rees songs — historical context

sources.title: Evangelische Gezangen — collection-level record (1806)

sources.title: Abraham Rutgers — historical biographical dictionary entry

sources.title: Afrikaans Lied 276 — modern source-chain page
sources.type: Modern institutional song page with an adaptation chain

limits: This is secondary chain evidence, not the physical witness for each intermediary edition. Modern Afrikaans lyrics and recordings have separate rights. The melody associated with the modern song must not be attributed as Lodenstein's original tune without a primary witness.

sources.title: Afrikaans Lied 271 — modern source-chain page

sources.title: I. Hert-sterckte in Jehova — 1676 print, printed pp. 78-81
sources.type: Exact text pages of the first edition, as served by the DBNL diplomatic transcription
supports: Full 15-stanza text of poem I in the 1676 print
Tune direction: 'Te singen als Onherroepelijke Jeugd! Of: Gavotte. A la fronté.'
Closing date line: 'Op 't Fort Nieuw Rees 28. in wintermaand 1673.'
Section heading tying the poem to the author's exile in Cleves
limits: A diplomatic transcription, not an inspected page image; no editorial intervention is listed for these pages, which is a positive but not sufficient accuracy signal.
The URL slug 0038 is a chunk number, not the printed page; cite printed pages.

sources.title: II. Hert-sterckte in Jehova — 1676 print, printed pp. 82-84
sources.type: Exact text pages of the first edition, as served by the DBNL diplomatic transcription
supports: Full 14-stanza text of poem II in the 1676 print
Tune direction: a pointer to I on p. 78 ('Te singen als boven pag.78. Soet Geselschap dat met my, &c.'), not an independent melody
Closing date line as emended by the transcription: 'Op 't Fort Nieuw Rees 4. In Loumaand 1674.'
Explicit 1676 pairing of the two poems of the same title
limits: The 1674 reading on this page is an editorial emendation; the DBNL colophon lists 'p. 84: 1664 -> 1674'. The printed original has not been visually inspected, so this page cannot by itself prove what the 1676 leaf reads.
The URL slug 0039 is a chunk number, not the printed page.

sources.title: 't Verheven Herte van een Christen die Gode leeft — 1676 print, printed pp. 85-87

Seven-line stanza with a divided second line, the metrical shape shared by item 32

sources.title: Uytspanningen, behelsende eenige stichtelyke liederen, en andere gedichten — 9th edition (1727)
sources.type: A separate later edition of the same collection, independently typeset
supports: An independent printed witness for the II. Hert-sterckte date reading '4 in Loumaand 1674' (printed p. 84)
Collation of Den Nederigen Christen (printed pp. 74-75), including the 1676/1727 variants recorded in the DUTCH-004 dossier
Continuity of the internal tune pointer 'siet boven pag. 29' at the same pagination
limits: A later edition is not independent of the 1676 text in stemmatic terms: it may descend from a corrected copy. It corroborates the date but cannot prove what the 1676 compositor set.
Its wording differs from 1676 in spelling and in the punctuation of Den Nederigen Christen stanza IV.

sources.title: Critical-edition introduction, 'Ds. Jodocus van Lodenstein en zijn Uyt-spanningen 1676', pp. 645-647
sources.type: Modern scholarly introduction in the copyrighted 2005 edition
supports: In December 1673 Lodenstein was held as a hostage of the French, far from Utrecht
He sent songs to the Utrecht circle, printed in 1674 as 'Meditatiën over eenige van Gods eygenschappen'
Many songs were written for singing in the Utrecht circle; melodies were drawn partly from popular 16th/17th-century tunes and partly from unidentified contemporary compositions
limits: Copyrighted secondary literature: paraphrase only, never quotation.
Describes the corpus generally; it does not date any individual poem.

sources.title: P.J. Buijnsters (ed.), Bloemlezing uit de bundel Uyt-spanningen (1971)
sources.type: Modern scholarly anthology with annotation
supports: Editorial headnote: four consolation songs written during the 1673 hostage period and published by the poet himself in 1674 as 'Meditatien over eenige van 's Heeren Gods Eygenschappen'
Footnote on the closing date of II: 'Er staat abusievelijk: 1664.' — an independent editorial statement that the print reads 1664
Printed reading '4. in Loumaand 1674' for II
limits: A later anthology, not the 1674 pamphlet or the 1676 leaf; the statement about the misprint is editorial testimony.
Copyrighted selection and annotation: cite, do not reproduce.

sources.title: Meditatien over eenige van 's Heeren Gods Eygenschappen (1674)
sources.type: The poet's own separate printing of the four exiled Rees hymns — target object
supports: Named by two independent modern descriptions (1971 headnote; 2005 introduction) as a 1674 printing of these songs
limits: No copy, catalogue record or locator has been acquired; its existence and contents are known only through secondary description.
Its collation against the 1676 printing is the strongest available test of the group's dating and remains outstanding.

sources.title: Nederlandse Liederenbank (Meertens Instituut / KNAW) — Dutch Song Database
sources.type: Scholarly song and melody index; the normal authority for Dutch tune designations
supports: Would carry the melody identification for tune names such as 'Prendete la', 'Onherroepelijke Jeugd' and 'Rosemont waer gy vliedt'
limits: Unavailable on 2026-10-25: the site returns HTTP 403 with a KNAW notice that it has been taken offline temporarily. DBNL's per-song links into it currently dead-end.
Not having consulted it is not evidence that a tune has no identification.
